assertion_analysis.regression: Make `ledger_generation` return the store's raw `"none"` instead of None: the first load records generation="none", the second compares it equal with the runs directory unchanged and reuses, so `gates[...] == "failed"` reds. The assertion is independent of the value under test (the edit is the source).

Key the generation path on the index directory again: `ledger_generation_path(PROJECT)` differs between the configured and fallback configurations, so the equality assertion reds before the write is even read back.
Remove the `_bump_generation` call at the end of `_restore_run_files`: `before` is now read immediately before the restore, so `after == before` and the assertion reds.

Remove the `_bump_generation` call in `_split_project_runs`: the assertion still passes, because no counter exists at any point in the case, so `reuse_documents` is false and the read walks the documents either way. Not independent of the code path it claims to guard.

baseline_suite.command: PYTHONPATH=<extracted tree> /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -n 4 <287 ledger-importing test paths>

findings.text: non-blocking: the split-read assertion cannot fail if the `_bump_generation` call in `_split_project_runs` (reckon/ledger.py:3309) is removed, because the fixture seeds the aggregate through `_write_json_envelope` and never advances the counter, so `generation is None` makes `reuse_documents` false and the read walks with or without the bump; capture `ledger_generation` before and after the split and assert it advanced before asserting the rows.

non-blocking: `_bump_generation` now delegates to `_store.advance_write_generation`, which suppresses OSError, where the pre-review implementation deleted the generation file on failure so a failed bump forced a rebuild; a failed advance leaves the counter matching the index and a warm read reuses stamps for a document edited in place, which is the staleness this key exists to prevent.

non-blocking: the fragment states the 2-at-20 and 2-at-200 figures for 'the same probe at the head commit', but reproduction.log's head probe ran at 1d2591f4, which the store-generation refactor at 4b4d91b4 superseded, so the fragment attributes a number to a head it was not measured at.

justifications.durability: test_a_ledger_no_write_has_touched_never_reuses_a_stale_index and test_a_write_is_seen_through_another_index_directory red when their fixes are reverted, but test_a_run_split_is_seen_by_the_next_read (tests/test_a_ledger_read_does_not_walk_every_run.py:313) passes with the split's bump at reckon/ledger.py:3309 removed.
justifications.evidence: the two-arm delta is empty and logged (arm-base.log, arm-head-fixed.log), but gate.log's 11 passed was run at 4b4d91b4 and reproduction.log's head probe at 1d2591f4, both superseded by fa88ae1a, so no single-file gate and no probe is recorded at the reviewed head.
justifications.fit: the helpers follow reckon/_store.py:1806's existing vocabulary and the new test isolates RECKON_HOME as tests/conftest.py does, though tests/test_a_ledger_read_does_not_walk_every_run.py:279 seeds through the private _store._write_json_envelope.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:1735-1740 keeps the read constant-cost at the reviewed head and the fa88ae1a arm passes the 20-vs-200 stat-count test, though the key sits in the store rather than beside the ledger as §64's deliverable words it.
justifications.reuse: ledger_generation and _bump_generation now wrap reckon/_store.py:1806-1847's write_generation_path, read_write_generation and advance_write_generation, the owner already consumed at reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py:245 and reckon/crew/obligations.py:1648, so the capability the prior review found forked is extended instead.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches only reckon/ledger.py, tests/test_a_ledger_read_does_not_walk_every_run.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/a-ledger-read-does-not-walk-every-run.html, each inside the declared write paths.
